topic: The Knowledge Vault: How MLP Layers Store Facts in Transformers
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of neural networks

outline.topic: The Knowledge Vault: How MLP Layers Store Facts in Transformers
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of neural networks

sections.title: The Architecture Landscape (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Define the Transformer's two main components: Attention (the router) and MLPs (the storage). Introduce the metaphor of a library where Attention finds the book, but the MLP contains the ink on the pages.
sections.example: Imagine a librarian (Attention) finding the encyclopedia on 'Mammals', while the MLP is the specific paragraph inside defining what a 'Dog' is.

sections.title: The Key-Value Memory Mechanism (0:45-2:00)
sections.content: Explain the MLP as a collection of 'Key-Value' memories. Visualize a matrix multiplication as an operation where input vectors (keys) are matched against stored patterns, triggering an output vector (value) that reinforces a specific fact.
sections.example: Visualizing a grid of light bulbs: Inputting 'Tokyo' activates a specific pattern of lights that, when summed, glows with the brightness of 'Japan'.

sections.title: Weight Updates: Writing the Fact (2:00-3:30)
sections.content: Describe how gradient descent 'writes' facts into weights. When the model sees (Subject: Paris, Relation: Capital Of, Object: France), it modifies the MLP weights to bridge these concepts. Explain this as adjusting the 'stiffness' of a connection.
sections.example: Using a slider analogy: Adjusting a fader on a mixing board until the output 'France' becomes louder when 'Paris' is triggered.

sections.title: Retrieval and Generalization (3:30-4:30)
sections.content: Explain how the model generalizes. Because facts are stored as distributed weights, the model can infer relationships it hasn't seen explicitly, effectively 'reasoning' through overlapping patterns in the vector space.
sections.example: If the model knows 'A tiger is a cat' and 'Cats are mammals', the overlapping activation patterns allow the model to categorize the tiger correctly without a direct database lookup.

sections.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
sections.content: Recap: Attention is for context, MLPs are for static knowledge. Final note on how this makes models 'black boxes'—it's hard to find the specific neuron that stores 'the capital of France' because the knowledge is diffused.
sections.example: Comparing the MLP to a hologram: You can break off a piece of the film (the weights), and you still see the whole image, just slightly blurrier.

storyboard.title: The Architecture Landscape (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Attention layers act as dynamic routers.
MLP layers act as static storage.
MLPs hold our deep knowledge base.
animations: Display two boxes: #3498db Router (Attention) and #e74c3c Storage (MLP).
Show blue glowing particles flowing dynamically into the Router box.
Show static, structured data blocks inside the red Storage box.
Animate blue particles connecting to specific static data points.
Highlight the red Storage box with pulsing light to represent stored knowledge.

storyboard.title: The Key-Value Memory Mechanism (0:45-2:00)
animations: Show a matrix of input vectors meeting a matrix of stored keys.
Visualize specific pairs flashing in matching colors (e.g., #2ecc71).
Show the resulting value vectors aggregating into a memory output.

storyboard.title: Weight Updates: Writing the Fact (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Gradient descent writes facts into weights.
animations: Display a sliding bar representing model weights, initially at neutral position.
Show a 'force' arrow pulling the bar toward a target value.
Lock the bar into a slightly adjusted position to reflect learning.

storyboard.title: Retrieval and Generalization (3:30-4:30)
animations: Visualize sparse dots distributed across a 2D plane.
Show overlapping ripples expanding from different dots, creating combined patterns.
Show two distant patterns merging to form a new, inferred concept.

storyboard.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Neurons are not single fact holders.
animations: Show an object casting a complex hologram of scattered light.
Slowly remove parts of the light while the full image remains visible.
Fade out the hologram to reveal the uniform, interconnected network behind it.
